newsitem.title: USA: Summers said growth signs in Russia encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Summers said growth signs in Russia encouraging.

text.p: U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers Thursday said that he was encouraged by some signs that the Russian economy might be turning around.

In a briefing at the Foreign Press Center, Summers said there was a need for the country to get to a point where economic growth was clearly established "although the signs in recent months have been encouraging."

He said it was crucial now that Russia has privatized so much of its economy that it enforce private contracts, protect property rights, maintain law and order and collect taxes in a fair and equitable manner.
"Those are very important challenges facing the government of Russia in the year ahead," he said.

He noted that there substantial progress on inflation, which he said was lower than many would have thought conceivable in the past. He also said that Russia now has more of its economy in the private sector than many countries in Western Europe.
